title: Should `<template for>` patch when `shadowrootmode` doesn't attach a shadow root?

labels.name: topic: shadow
labels.description: Relates to shadow trees (as defined in DOM)

body:
### What is the issue with the HTML Standard?

The `template` start tag steps in ["in head"](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/parsing.html#parsing-main-inhead) give a valid `shadowrootmode` precedence over `for`, even when no shadow root gets attached:

> If *template*'s `shadowrootmode` attribute is not in the None state:
>
> 1. If any of the following are true:
>    - the parser's allow declarative shadow roots is false;
>    - *hostIsRoot* is true; or
>    - the parser's insertion target redirection map[*declarativeShadowHostElement*] exists,
>
>    then insert an element at the adjusted insertion location with *template*, *insertionLocation*, and true, and return.
>
> ...
>
> Otherwise, if *template* has a `for` attribute: ...

Attaching the shadow root can also fail, in which case the steps likewise insert *template* and return. So per spec, `for` is ignored whenever `shadowrootmode` is valid.

Chrome Canary 157 patches instead whenever no shadow root is attached:

```js
const div = document.createElement("div");
div.innerHTML = '<?marker name="x"><template shadowrootmode=open for=x>A</template>';
div.innerHTML;
// Spec: '<?marker name="x"?><template shadowrootmode="open" for="x">A</template>'
// Chrome Canary 157: 'A'
```

The same happens with a top-level template in `setHTMLUnsafe()`, and with `Document.parseHTMLUnsafe()` when the host already has a shadow root. Chrome only skips patching when the shadow root is attached. Gecko's in-progress implementation ([bug 2053472](https://bugzilla.mozilla.org/show_bug.cgi?id=2053472)) does the same as Chrome. [template-for-superseded-by-shadowrootmode.html](https://github.com/web-platform-tests/wpt/blob/master/html/semantics/scripting-1/the-template-element/template-for/template-for-superseded-by-shadowrootmode.html) only covers the case where the shadow root is attached.

Maybe the spec should match: fall through to the `for` steps when no shadow root is attached, instead of returning.

cc @foolip @noamr
